function.name: launch_or_open
function.description: Open a program, a website or a FILE on this PC by name. Examples: steam, discord, notepad, spotify, youtube, github, google, wikipedia. You may name several, e.g. 'steam and youtube'. Files: give a workspace file like 'ad.html', 'out/report.pdf' or 'result.png' (absolute paths also work) - it opens with the default program (HTML/PDF/PNG open in the browser). The tool decides whether each name is an app, a workspace file or a website.

name.description: Name of the program or website to open.

function.name: list_dir
function.description: List files and folders inside the workspace folder (paths are relative to it). Use before reading files so you know what exists.

path.description: Relative path inside the workspace, e.g. 'src', '' (default = workspace root).

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read a text file inside the workspace folder (relative path). Returns its full content.

path.description: Relative path of the file, e.g. 'notes.txt'.

function.name: search_files
function.description: Regex search across files in the workspace folder and returns file + line matches.

path.description: Optional relative folder to search inside (default = whole workspace).

function.name: write_file
function.description: Create or overwrite a text file inside the workspace folder (relative path). Creates parent folders if missing. Use only when the user asks you to write or create a file.

function.name: edit_file
function.description: Replace text inside an existing file in the workspace folder (relative path). Replaces ALL occurrences of old_text with new_text.

function.name: web_search
function.description: Search the internet when you need up-to-date information, facts, news, documentation or anything you are not sure about. Returns a short list of titles, links and snippets. Then read details with web_fetch on the most relevant link.

query.description: Search query, e.g. 'latest node.js LTS version'.

function.name: web_fetch
function.description: Fetch and read the full text of a webpage by URL. Use after web_search to read an article, docs page or answer in detail.

function.name: run_command
function.description: Run a shell command on this Windows PC and return its output. Use it to build, test, install, debug or check system info: python, pip, git, npm, node, dir, tasklist, systeminfo, ping, etc. Runs in the workspace folder by default. Max 45 seconds by default - raise 'timeout' for long-running commands (up to 600s). Output truncated to ~8 KB. In PLAN mode this tool is disabled.

command.description: The command to run, e.g. 'python tools/screenshot.py'.

workdir.description: Optional folder to run in: absolute path or relative to the workspace. Default = workspace root.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in seconds (1-600). Use a higher value for long downloads, builds or tests. Default 45.

function.name: run_code
function.description: Run a snippet in a sandboxed environment and return its output. Languages available on this PC are auto-detected - typically: python, node (JavaScript). Also supported when installed: go, lua, php, ruby, perl, bash. Use it to test functions, verify logic, parse data or prototype before touching real files. Runs in an isolated temp folder that is deleted afterwards. Default timeout 30s, up to 600s.

language.description: Language to run: 'python', 'node' (or 'js'), 'go', 'lua', 'php', 'ruby', 'perl', 'bash'. If the runtime is missing this returns the list actually available.

timeout.description: Max seconds to run (1-600). Default 30. Raise it for slow work, e.g. simulations.

function.name: take_screenshot
function.description: Capture the screen (or a region of it) and SEE it - you have vision, so the image is fed directly to your eyes. Use this whenever you need to inspect what is displayed on the PC: error dialogs, app windows, web pages, terminal output, a GUI, or to check the result of your own mouse/keyboard actions. Also saves the PNG inside the workspace so the user has a copy.

region.description: Optional region to capture: {x, y, width, height} in screen pixels. Omit for the full screen (all monitors).

function.name: control_input
function.description: Control the mouse and keyboard like a human: move the cursor, click, double-click, right-click, drag, scroll, type text or send key combinations. Pair it with take_screenshot to see the result. Coordinates are screen pixels (0,0 = top-left of the primary monitor).

action.description: What to do. 'move' only moves the cursor. 'click'/'double_click'/'right_click' move then click. 'drag' moves then drags the mouse button. 'scroll' scrolls. 'type' writes text. 'keys' presses each key. 'hotkey' presses keys together.

x.description: Cursor X (screen pixel). Not needed for 'type'/'keys'/'hotkey'.

y.description: Cursor Y (screen pixel). Not needed for 'type'/'keys'/'hotkey'.

amount.description: For 'scroll': number of scroll steps (negative = down).

function.name: clipboard
function.description: Read or write the system clipboard. Use 'get' to read what the user copied, and 'set' to put text on the clipboard so the user can paste it anywhere.

action.description: 'get' reads the current clipboard text; 'set' writes 'text' to the clipboard.

text.description: Required for 'set': the text to copy.

function.name: download_file
function.description: Download a file from a web URL and save it inside the workspace folder. Returns the saved path, the byte size and (for text files) the beginning of the content so you can see what you got.

path.description: Relative destination inside the workspace, e.g. 'Downloads/installer.exe'. Defaults to the file name from the URL.

function.name: archive
function.description: Create or extract archives (zip / tar / tar.gz / tgz) inside the workspace folder. Use 'extract' to unpack a file into a folder, or 'create' to pack files/folders into a new zip.

action.description: 'extract' unpacks 'archive' into 'dest'. 'create' packs 'files' into a new archive.

archive.description: Relative path of the archive (for extract: the file to unpack; for create: the file to produce).

dest.description: For 'extract': relative folder to unpack into. For 'create': optional destination file.

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Ask the user a question and wait for their answer, like a human would. Use it when you need a choice, extra information, a password, or confirmation before doing something important. The user can pick one of the given options or type a free answer. The rest of your work is paused until they reply.

question.description: The question to ask, phrased clearly.

options.description: Optional short answer options the user can pick with one click.

function.name: todo_write
function.description: Replace the visible TODO list with the given items and statuses. Use it at the start of a longer task to show the user the plan, and update it as you make progress. Status can be 'pending', 'in_progress' or 'completed'.

todos.description: The full new list of todo items.

function.name: window_list
function.description: List the open desktop windows: window title, process name and PID for every visible top-level window. Use this first to discover what is running, then bring one to the front with window_action.

function.name: window_action
function.description: Control an existing desktop window: bring a window to the front and give it keyboard focus, maximize it, minimize it or restore it. Find a matching window first with window_list. The window can be matched by a substring of its title ('title') or by its process name/PID ('process'/'pid'). 'focus' makes the window visible, restores it if minimized and steals focus so that take_screenshot/control_input act on it.

action.description: What to do with the window. Default: focus.

title.description: Substring of the window title to match.

function.name: docker_ps
function.description: List Docker containers. Include stopped ones with 'all'. Returns id, name, image and status per container. Use docker_logs/docker_exec/docker_start/docker_stop with the returned names.

function.name: docker_images
function.description: List Docker images available locally (repository, tag, id, size).

function.name: docker_start
function.description: Start a Docker container by name or id.

function.name: docker_stop
function.description: Stop a running Docker container by name or id.

function.name: docker_restart
function.description: Restart a Docker container by name or id.

function.name: docker_logs
function.description: Read the logs of a Docker container by name or id.

tail.description: Number of lines from the end (default 100).

function.name: docker_exec
function.description: Run a command inside a running Docker container (docker exec with sh -c). Returns the command output.

command.description: The shell command to run inside the container, e.g. 'ls -la /app'.

function.name: api_call
function.description: Make an HTTP request to any REST or GraphQL API and read the response: status code, headers and body. Works for GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE/HEAD/OPTIONS. For GraphQL send a JSON body like {"query": "..."} - the response JSON is returned automatically. Handles JSON bodies from dict input, or raw text bodies.

body.description: Request body. Use a dict/list for JSON or a string for raw text.

function.name: ws_test
function.description: Connect to a WebSocket server, optionally send a message, and collect the replies that arrive before the timeout. Useful to test APIs, push feeds, or debug local sockets.

url.description: WebSocket URL, e.g. ws://127.0.0.1:8000/ws or wss://...

send.description: Optional message to send after connecting. Dicts/lists are JSON-encoded.

timeout.description: How long to listen for replies, seconds (default 5, max 60).

function.name: schedule_task
function.description: Schedule a shell command to run later (and while this PC is on): once after a delay, on an interval, or on a cron schedule. Intervals are 'every N seconds'. Cron is a 5-field expression: minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week (0 or 7 = Sunday). Examples: '15 3 * * *' daily at 03:15; '*/5 * * * *' every 5 minutes; '0 9 * * 1-5' weekdays at 09:00. The command runs via the system shell (cmd). Check runs with list_schedules; cancel with unschedule_task.

delay_seconds.description: For 'once': seconds to wait before running (default 1).

timeout.description: Max seconds the command may run (default 180, max 600).

function.name: list_schedules
function.description: List all scheduled tasks: name, schedule kind, next run time, last run, how many times it ran and the tail of its last output.

function.name: unschedule_task
function.description: Cancel a scheduled task by name. Already-started runs are not interrupted.

function.name: tts_voices
function.description: List the local Piper text-to-speech voices available on this machine (each .onnx + .onnx.json pair in the Piper folder). Use tts_speak with one of the returned names.

function.name: tts_speak
function.description: Speak text aloud using the local neural Piper TTS engine (no cloud, no Windows voices). Also saves the speech as a WAV file in the workspace. Use this to give the user spoken feedback, alerts or TTS output.

voice.description: Piper voice name, default 'en_US-lessac-medium'. Romanian: 'ro_RO-mihai-medium'. List with tts_voices.

function.name: preview_html
function.description: Live-preview an HTML page you created in the workspace. Call it after writing an .html/.htm file (e.g. a chart, a report or a small web app) - the UI will show a live iframe of the page. The page is served from this PC, so JavaScript and local assets work. Returns the preview URL.

path.description: Relative workspace path of the .html/.htm file, e.g. 'out/report.html'.
